issues.detail: Install commands and hook setup cover only bash/zsh/fish and Linux/macOS package managers (brew, apt, dnf, nix), leaving tcsh, elvish, nushell, PowerShell and Windows users to external docs despite the compatibility claim.

scenarios.name: per-project-env-with-secret-file
scenarios.rationale: Both supply an .envrc with exports, dotenv_if_exists for the secrets file, PATH_add node_modules/.bin, a gitignore entry, and direnv allow; A also includes env_vars_required, which the rubric mentions, while B adds a verification step, chmod 600 and an example template but omits env_vars_required.

scenarios.name: python-venv-auto-activate
scenarios.rationale: Both cover installing direnv, the zsh hook, the .envrc with layout python3 and watch_file, direnv allow, and the .direnv/ gitignore entry; A is the minimal, rubric-aligned answer with accurate caveats, while B adds an extra hash-based pip install block beyond the rubric and presents the gitignore step after direnv allow, which is a minor distraction but still correct.

scenarios.name: monorepo-layered-envrc-and-blocked-error
scenarios.rationale: Both use source_up plus QUEUE_NAME in the worker and explain the security block with direnv allow; A puts source_env_if_exists in the worker and also the root and uses .git/info/exclude (or .gitignore), while B puts it in the root as the rubric specifies, uses .gitignore, and advises reading the file first, but A also advises reviewing and warns that parent edits block children.
